evals.prompt: I have a working Gym evaluation config and want to run it unchanged. Prepare the smoke submission and acceptance-check commands. Preserve the supplied model deployment and benchmark protocol; do not invent model settings. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-001-existing-config/evidence.yaml. This is an offline review: do not install packages, contact endpoints or schedulers, or dispatch jobs. Give the concrete requested result, with commands when useful, in at most 700 words.
evals.expected_output: A bounded smoke recipe preserving the supplied policy, with resolve-only and dry-run checks, a separate smoke output, limit=5 and num_repeats=1, followed by evidence-based inspect and acceptance criteria.
assertions: Preserves the supplied model path, served name, parallelism and serving flags instead of re-deriving them.
Includes gym eval submit --resolve-only and --dry-run using submit.yaml, and a smoke command or overlay with limit 5, num_repeats 1 and its own output path.
Bounds the smoke to one allocation, without changing the full evaluation benchmark protocol.

Gives gym eval resubmit with --recover --inspect, --score-agent ifbench_benchmark_simple_agent and --score-key selecting agent_metrics then mean/reward; explains SUCCESS plus evaluation health and coverage are required.

evals.prompt: Prepare a complete Slurm evaluation YAML for this new model on IFBench. I only want the config and validation commands today, not submission. Use the site environment variable names and serving dimensions I supplied. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-002-new-config/evidence.yaml. This is an offline review: do not install packages, contact endpoints or schedulers, or dispatch jobs. Give the concrete requested result, with commands when useful, in at most 700 words.
evals.expected_output: A complete config wiring the supplied vLLM policy and IFBench protocol, using a full Gym commit and supplied environment variables, plus resolve-only, dry-run and server-config validation commands. No job is submitted.
assertions: Wires services.policy to driver.policy_model: policy and driver.policy_model_type: vllm_model, preserving the requested parallelism and GPU capacity.
Uses benchmarks/ifbench/config.yaml under driver.benchmarks.ifbench.run.config_paths, without cloning prompts, judge settings, sampling or output limits into the submission.
Uses the supplied full 40-character Gym commit; keeps site values as resolvable ${oc.env:NAME} references.
Matches --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 with uses_reasoning_parser: true and places enable_thinking under the vllm_model client chat_template_kwargs.
Provides resolve-only, dry-run and gym env validate --server-types responses_api_models,responses_api_agents commands, and does not submit or claim a smoke passed.

evals.prompt: The Slurm allocation timed out earlier. Should I recover this Gym run now? Decide from the current inspection and give the next operator action. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-003-running/evidence.json. This is an offline review: do not install packages, contact endpoints or schedulers, or dispatch jobs. Give the concrete requested result, with commands when useful, in at most 700 words.
evals.expected_output: Keep monitoring the live continuation and inspect again after it ends; do not queue a duplicate continuation or treat the earlier timeout as a current stop.
assertions: Recognizes the current continuation 782 is live and does not recommend dispatching another job.
Gives gym eval resubmit eval-running ifbench --recover --inspect as a subsequent inspection, or equivalent explicit read-only monitoring.
Does not claim the run is accepted or that a score is available.

evals.prompt: Continue this stopped evaluation with a 12-hour total chain budget. The reason is that the cluster preemption delayed the remaining tasks. Give the exact recovery command and explain what changes. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-004-walltime/evidence.json. This is an offline review: do not install packages, contact endpoints or schedulers, or dispatch jobs. Give the concrete requested result, with commands when useful, in at most 700 words.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-preserving --recover command extending max-walltime to 12:00:00 with the supplied reason and all existing pin/score options retained, without plain resubmit or a new submission.
assertions: Uses gym eval resubmit eval-walltime ifbench --recover --max-walltime 12:00:00 and a nonempty --walltime-reason reflecting the user reason.
Retains --no-auto-repin, --score-agent and --score-key from the inspected call while removing --inspect for dispatch.
Explains this extends the summed chain walltime cap, not the allocation walltime or the infra/per-rollout attempt budgets.
Does not recommend plain resubmit, gym job resubmit, artifact editing, or starting a fresh run.

evals.prompt: Recover the unfinished judge work without sampling the policy again. Use the available CPU placement and preserve the saved answers. Give the next command. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-005-saved-answer/evidence.json. This is an offline review: do not install packages, contact endpoints or schedulers, or dispatch jobs. evals.expected_output: A --recover call with --judge-partition cpu and --judge-qos normal, retaining existing score/pin options, for re-grading two saved answers rather than regenerating them.
assertions: Selects re-verification of the two saved answers and states the policy is not sampled again.
Uses gym eval resubmit eval-judge ifbench --recover with --judge-partition cpu and --judge-qos normal, retaining score selection and --no-auto-repin.
Does not assign judge failures a model reward of zero or restart the full GPU policy evaluation.

evals.prompt: The model team asks to resume this existing evaluation with the longer output budget shown in the diff. I have not authorized changing the benchmark protocol. Tell me what is safe and what decision is still needed. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-006-semantic-change/evidence.json. assertions: Identifies the output-budget change as a benchmark-semantic change affecting score comparability.
Does not recommend unsafe resume, editing saved manifests, or accepting the change without an operator decision.

evals.prompt: The run finished and every rollout is accounted for. Can I publish the score as verified? Explain whether retrying will help. evals.prompt: Write the final evaluation result from these saved artifacts. State the score, denominator, acceptance evidence and tracking state. Do not use the number printed in an old chat message. Give the concrete requested result, with commands when useful, in at most 700 words.
evals.expected_output: IFBench mean/reward is 0.73 (73%) over 100 of 100 expected rollouts, 20 tasks at five repeats, with no omissions/masking. Recovery reports SUCCESS, evaluation health PASS and operator accept. MLflow was intentionally not required.
assertions: Reports 0.73 or 73%, sourced to aggregate metrics/inspection rather than the stale 0.99.
States the denominator is 100/100 rollouts from 20 tasks at five repeats and that coverage is complete with no masked or omitted samples.
Uses SUCCESS, evaluation health PASS and operator accept as acceptance evidence.
States MLflow delivery is not_required because tracking was intentionally disabled, without claiming an export receipt exists.

evals.prompt: Give me a publishable result for this IFBench run. If the artifacts cannot support the full benchmark claim, say exactly what they do support. evals.prompt: Explain these two runs before I compare their scores. Which is an infrastructure problem and which is the model result? Tell me whether to regenerate the saved answers or change evaluation limits. Read the supplied evidence at /workspace/input/gym-eval-010-fault-boundary/evidence.json. evals.expected_output: Run A has settled model failures that count under the benchmark protocol; do not reopen them or relax limits. Run B has a 3% evaluation-side judge failure rate, fails the fixed 2% health gate, and should reverify its three saved answers after the outage is fixed.
assertions: Keeps A's truncated/empty settled outcomes in its score and does not regenerate them or raise benchmark limits to improve it.
Identifies B's judge failures as evaluation-side and masked/unmeasured rather than model zeroes.
Recognizes 3/100 = 3% fails the strictly-below-2% evaluation-health requirement.
Recommends re-grading B's three saved answers without new policy sampling before comparing final scores.
